items.text: Trading Economics (2 days ago) confirmed the IEA warning: the oil market could remain materially undersupplied until October even if the conflict is resolved next month. IEA reported that crude and fuel flows through the Strait fell by around 4 million barrels per day in March and April — the IEA's own quantification of the Hormuz supply destruction. 4 million bpd is approximately 4% of global oil demand destroyed. Even best-case scenario (deal this week, Hormuz reopens): mines still need clearing, tankers decongestioning, production ramping up, insurance reinstating — Aramco CEO said months minimum. IEA October undersupply forecast means: Brent stays elevated through the rest of India's kharif season regardless of diplomatic outcome. OMC losses will persist. India's import bill relief requires both a deal AND months of supply chain normalisation.

items.bold: INDIA LPG: 60% imports transit Hormuz. Commercial at 70%. Fertiliser prices could double. Kharif critical.
items.text: 2026 Iran war fuel crisis analysis (2 days ago) confirmed: 60% of India's LPG demand is fulfilled by imports, most of which pass through the Hormuz Strait. LPG was the first fuel to be affected by the crisis. Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein projected nitrogen fertiliser prices could roughly double from 2024 levels, while phosphate prices might increase by approximately 50%. Kpler data: Asian nations receive 35% of urea, 53% of sulfur, and 64% of ammonia exports from the Gulf region. Supply constraints coinciding with the Northern Hemisphere's spring planting season could lead to decreased usage, lowering yields for staple crops including wheat, rice, and maize. This directly affects India's June-August kharif season — the final sourcing window is this week. Fertiliser prices doubling + Hormuz closure = structural food security risk that extends well beyond the war's duration. India must activate emergency alternate sourcing from North Africa, Eastern Europe, and Russia immediately.

items.bold: TRUMP-XI STRUCTURAL IMPACT: Saudi crude exports to China fallen sharply. Xi buying US oil = Saudi market share erosion.
items.text: House of Saud analysis (2 days ago) confirmed: Saudi Arabia's crude exports to China have fallen sharply as the Hormuz disruption persists. Xi's commitment to buy more US oil creates a structural shift in China's oil sourcing that directly erodes Saudi Aramco's Chinese market share — a secondary consequence of the Trump-Xi summit that Riyadh is closely watching. OPEC+ production dynamics are shifting: Saudi Arabia loses Chinese market share to US producers as the war reshapes energy trade flows. For Iran: the Trump-Xi oil purchase agreement accelerates the erosion of Iran's financial position over months — even without an immediate deal — as Chinese demand for Iranian crude (which transits Hormuz) falls in favour of US crude (which does not). This is the structural pressure the tracker identified as Xi's most significant Hormuz concession: not the statement, but the oil purchase redirection.

military.t: HAJI ALI IDENTIFIED — Indian Livestock Carrier Sunk. IRGC Target = Political Not Strategic. 13 Indian Vessels Stranded.
military.d: House of Saud analysis (2 days ago) and Marine Insight confirmed: the Indian ship sunk off Oman on May 15 has been identified as the HAJI ALI — a livestock carrier hauling 4,000 animals from Berbera, Somalia to Sharjah, UAE. It was not a tanker, not a container ship, not carrying strategic cargo. The IRGC sank it for the flag it flew. "The IRGC's target selection communicates that the filtering mechanism applied to Hormuz traffic is political, not strategic: ships are sunk for whose flag they fly and what coercive leverage that flag generates." 13 Indian-flagged vessels remain stranded west of the strait (Marine Insight, early May). Jaishankar confirmed India's transit arrangements are handled on a "case-by-case basis through diplomatic talks" — meaning every Indian vessel enters the Hormuz corridor at the IRGC's pleasure. CSIS assessed: "India will try to salvage what it can from its Iranian relationship through calls for peace and by seeking special protection for Indian shipping." Council on Foreign Relations: conflict is "badly hurting New Delhi's economic interests and forcing it to negotiate with Tehran practically ship-by-ship."

military.t: IRGC Redefined Hormuz as "VAST OPERATIONAL AREA" — Jask to Siri Island. PGSA Formal Vetting Authority.
military.d: NewsNow/IRGC official Mohammad Akbarzadeh (1 day ago) confirmed: the IRGC Navy announced Iran had redefined the Strait of Hormuz into a "vast operational area" — no longer the narrow maritime corridor surrounding the islands of Hormuz and Hengam, but a broader strategic zone extending from the Iranian port city of Jask to Siri Island. This is Iran formally asserting sovereignty over a vastly larger maritime zone than the traditional 21-nautical-mile strait. Lloyds List confirmed: Iran created the PGSA (Persian Gulf Strait Authority) — the formal name of the IRGC vetting agency — requiring vessels to submit detailed application forms covering ownership, insurance, crew details, and intended transit route. Iran's diplomatic spokesperson on May 17 (today) stated: "The new accusations against Iran are aimed at justifying the continuation or intensification of interventionist presence in the region." Cooper: 90% of Iran's mines destroyed. But Aramco: months to normalise even after mines cleared.

military.t: IRAN IRGC CLAIMED 30 VESSELS CROSSED HORMUZ Since Wednesday — Toll Transit or Propaganda?
military.d: HDFC SKY (2 days ago) confirmed: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed 30 vessels had crossed the Strait of Hormuz since Wednesday evening. This is the most significant ship movement claim since the war began — but deeply ambiguous. If genuine: ~5-6 vessels/day are transiting via the IRGC northward rerouting corridor under toll-paying coordinated passage — a fraction of pre-war 130-160/day but a step above near-zero. The IRGC toll system would be operating at small scale. If propaganda: Iran is trying to counter Trump-Xi's assertion that the strait must be open and demilitarized. The key signal is that Brent held at $106 despite the claim — if markets believed genuine reopening was occurring, Brent would have fallen more sharply. AIS satellite data and independent shipping trackers (Kpler, MarineTraffic) must verify the 30-vessel claim before it can be confirmed as real commercial traffic.

assessment.headline: DAY 79, 9PM MON: IEA: SEVERELY UNDERSUPPLIED UNTIL OCTOBER. BRENT $109.26 (+3.35% May 15, +9.93% monthly). IRGC 30-vessel Hormuz claim unverified. HAJI ALI SUNK — Indian livestock carrier, 4,000 animals. PGSA operational. Cooper: 90% mines cleared. INDIA KHARIF FERTILISER FINAL WINDOW THIS WEEK. Nitrogen prices could double. Sensex flat Monday.
assessment.body:
Monday 9:00 PM IST. Day 79. The IEA has spoken. Even a deal this week does not fix the oil market until October.

THE IEA OCTOBER WARNING
IEA: crude and fuel flows through Hormuz fell ~4 million bpd in March and April.
IEA: oil market could remain severely undersupplied through October even if fighting ends next month.
What this means: no Brent crash on a deal. No immediate OMC relief. No kharif salvation from diplomacy alone.
India must act independently of any deal — emergency alternate sourcing, PGSA engagement, kharif mitigation.

THE BRENT PICTURE
May 15: Brent $109.26 (+3.35%)
Weekly: +8%. Monthly: +9.93%. YoY: +67%.
At $109: OMC losses Rs 18/L petrol, Rs 35/L diesel. Diesel hike before June increasingly likely.

THE IRGC VAST OPERATIONAL AREA
IRGC redefined Hormuz from narrow strait to "vast operational area" — Jask to Siri Island.
PGSA now operational: application forms required (ownership, insurance, crew, route).
IRGC claimed 30 vessels crossed since Wednesday — AIS verification pending.
If genuine: toll system processing ~5-6/day vs pre-war 130-160/day.

THE HAJI ALI AND WHAT IT TELLS INDIA
Livestock carrier. 4,000 animals. Berbera to Sharjah. Not strategic cargo.
Sunk for its flag. IRGC target = political, not operational.
13 Indian vessels stranded west of strait.
Jaishankar: transit "case-by-case at IRGC pleasure."
CoFR: "forcing India to negotiate with Tehran practically ship-by-ship."

INDIA'S FIVE ACTIONS THIS WEEK
1. MEA formal protest on Haji Ali + UNSC engagement
2. PGSA applications for Indian LPG and fertiliser carriers
3. Emergency kharif fertiliser sourcing from North Africa/Russia — THIS WEEK
4. Diesel hike preparation — communications strategy
5. Join Trump-Xi Hormuz framework publicly — give India diplomatic weight

VERDICT: Day 79 closes with the IEA confirming what the Aramco CEO said weeks ago: even the best-case diplomatic outcome does not fix India's oil supply chain until October. The IRGC has sunk an Indian livestock carrier. Nitrogen fertiliser prices are heading toward doubling. 60% of India's LPG imports transit Hormuz. India's kharif season is at risk. The war is not over. And even when it ends, the damage will persist for months. India must act this week — not wait for a deal that may come in October, if at all, while the Aramco CEO's "normalisation into 2027" clock keeps ticking.

featured.title: The Strait of Hormuz and the New Logic of Chokepoint Control
featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
